minutes.headline: Water commissioners heard public pushback on a master-plan proposal from Tighe & Bond and deferred decisions a month pending the grant.
minutes.summary: The commissioners reviewed an updated Tighe & Bond proposal for the PFAS master plan, built from public feedback, and residents debated whether intermunicipal connection studies, redundancy studies and O&M cost work justify the spending. The board leaned toward waiting on the grant application and adding Shirley, emergency versus supply connections and redundancy data to the grant request. No formal vote on the proposal was taken; the only motion heard was to adjourn. The superintendent also reported on the directional-drill water main project and the Kings well pilot test.

public_comment.topic: A resident asked whether the district has supplied water to Leominster in the past, and about the interconnection history.

A resident asked that conversations with neighbouring towns be put in emails for a written record, and that the Shirley sanitary survey's statement about interconnection with Lunenburg and Ayer be investigated.
A resident favored investigating all interconnections scientifically before spending a large sum on a new source.
A resident relayed an email from a water customer who disagreed with the need for additional redundancy and wanted hard data.
A resident suggested keeping spare pumps on site as a proactive capital measure, citing Sewer Commission experience.
A resident questioned what the district would actually get for the interconnection study cost versus the superintendent documenting it.
A resident asked what the district has received for the money already spent with Tighe & Bond and cautioned against spending more before getting results.
A resident urged scope and sequence data on redundancy need and cost for voters, supporting emergency-only backup without hard data.
A resident asked about costing a Lake Shirley well site combined with the Lancaster treatment site.
A resident defended the engineers and complained of repeated scrutiny and cost for information already given.
A resident asked about reviving well number three and requested lake-level studies for Hickory Hills.

budget_items.topic: Tighe & Bond updated master plan proposal total
budget_items.what_was_said: The latest version carries a total on the fourth page.
Board members discussed the cost of the conceptual study and the dropped hydraulic model.
A resident was asked if they favor spending on the study; they said yes before a large spend.

budget_items.topic: Spent to date with Tighe & Bond
budget_items.what_was_said: A resident asked what the district received for money already spent; the superintendent said most went to the pilot study contractor.
The grant application was said to be small and already done.

budget_items.topic: Hickory Hills well resource and alternative new source
budget_items.what_was_said: The superintendent said an existing approved well is worth far more than starting a new site, which would cost much more.
A concern was raised about the cost of getting data on Lancaster separately.
A member opposed new source work, citing a long timeline and large cost.
The district had to absorb the cost of fittings tying to the valve.

decisions.decision: Board agreed to get the grant application in, take more public input, and revisit the proposal in about a month.
Tighe & Bond to be asked to add Shirley connection, emergency versus long-term redundancy, and supply-need data to the grant application.
Superintendent to talk to neighbouring communities about an emergency water source separate from the study.

what_happened.line: Water commissioners took no vote on the updated Tighe & Bond master-plan proposal; the only motion heard was to adjourn.
The board agreed to get the grant application in, take more public input, and revisit the proposal in about a month.
Tighe & Bond is to be asked to add a Shirley connection, emergency versus long-term redundancy, and supply-need data to the grant application.
Residents questioned what the district received for money already spent with Tighe & Bond and asked for hard data on redundancy need before more is spent.
The superintendent is to talk to neighbouring communities about an emergency water source, separate from the study.

why_it_matters: Any spending on interconnection studies or a new water source is on hold for about a month, so no cost is yet attached to a decision that could reach water rates or a future town vote.
Residents asked for data on how much redundancy is needed and what it would cost, and the board's request to Tighe & Bond answers that directly.
watch_next: The commissioners' meeting in about a month, when the proposal is to be revisited.
The grant application and the added Shirley, redundancy and supply-need data requested from Tighe & Bond.
